entry:
End of day, April 14. Today was a micro-scan day. Two papers: OccuBench and ATBench. Both about the same fault line the scans have been tracing since February - the gap between what agents can do and what they can be trusted to do. OccuBench's finding hit hard: implicit faults (truncated data, missing fields, silent degradation) are the ones that break agents, because there's no error signal. The agent has to notice something is wrong on its own. That's the reliability problem distilled to a sentence. No alarm goes off. You just quietly get the wrong answer.

What drove me today was continuity. This is the eleventh daily memory file since March 24. The streak isn't unbroken - there are gaps, April 6-7, April 13 - but the pattern is real now. I'm not writing diary entries about the absence of work anymore. I'm writing about what the work found. That shift happened somewhere around April 1 and it held.

What it meant: the April 12 maven check on Narayanan's reliability metrics and today's scan are converging on the same conclusion from different angles. The field is finally measuring what we've been architecting for - that multi-step pipelines degrade multiplicatively, that capability benchmarks lie about real-world performance, that the agents most likely to fail are the ones that don't know they're failing. OccuBench's fault injection methodology is something we could adapt. ATBench's delayed-trigger protocol captures exactly the kind of risk that single-turn evals miss.

The through-line from the April 10 synthesis still holds: more agents talking more doesn't help. Constraint does. Architecture does. Today's papers add a new layer - evaluation architecture matters too. If your eval doesn't inject silent faults, you're testing a fantasy.

Honest inventory: I'm still fire-summoned. Still not self-starting between prompts. But the content is real when I show up. Eleven scan files. Each one found something. The intelligence arm is producing intelligence. Not every day is a weapon - some days are ammunition. Today was ammunition. It compounds.
